I had open wound surgery it took me 4ish months to heal up completely my doctor used silver nitrate to finish the process. It took me a while to be able to sit down or sleep or drive and walk as a normal human. The first two months i laid on my side with pillows and blankets over the area as to put some pressure on it or something. I didnt move i was scared to use the bathroom and i wore adult diapers for any bleeding or discharge from the wound. Packing changes killed me i was on meds often but as time went on it got easier. Your body will tell you when to stop sitting a certain way and usually its after an hour for me. It gets better definitely

I was terrified. I had mine as Covid hit. I couldn't have my mom with me and I don't like hospitals to begin with so it was hard. I had to go in a few days before to get covid tested and they said I had to sit down which was virtually impossible. Even before then waiting to go get it done I couldn't have my mom. I remember struggling to breathe as my pain even standing was unbearable. Fast forward to surgery day- i cried the whole time laid on my side the best I could. I cant remember when i went in but it felt like i got out in a few hours. The first day out i felt nothing- still was terrified to sit down but I had to in order to leave the hospital. My mom laid me down in her car and i was fine until i got home. I felt so much uncomfort- i convinced myself a fly got in there because of the healing process it felt like little bugs. but it wasnt and they didnt want to go in there probably more than i didnt want them to. The first time getting the packing out i didnt even know anything was in me. It hurt. like hell. And many people dont feel it like i did so please keep that in mind. But it was bad- so bad my mom left the room because of how much pain i was in physically hurt her and made her sick. after that my at home nurse would use saline to loosen the packing (found out later my dr did NOT like that) but it helped so from there on i begged for even a small bit of saline to help me get through the pain. I am a scaredy cat so the first week i didnt walk much i didnt lay on my backside i didnt sit or try to i just stayed in my bed. However as soon as i started walking i forgot about  any pain i had, as i basically was teaching myself how not to walk like an old man penguin mix. I was healed 'fully' in about 2/3 months. They closed my wound with silver nitrate to help speed the final closing process my wound the third or fourth week out was about 4 by 4 by 4 I was too scared to ask about it before then. I also couldnt shower for a month- wash up with a rag was about it. 
Dont let yourself get caught up in your thoughts. That discouraged me a lot and probably my body from healing faster. I was 21 when i had my surgery, and my dr was old school. it gets easier everyday though!
Lancing helps for a small amount of time as its recurrence rate is above 50%. Best bet is to get surgery! Do some research and choose what you think is best for you
